pages.text: "Dodo, someone's on the bridge!" Little brother Mumu hid behind his big sister. Grandma Duck crossed the bridge with a walking stick and a basket. Mumu peeped from behind Dodo's ribbon.
"Grandma!" Dodo ran into her wings. Grandma called, "Mumu has grown so much too!" He stepped back. "I want to go... but I'm not sure."
Grandma sat beside the straw pile, with Dodo snug beside her. Mumu watched from behind the pile. "Hello..." His greeting was very soft.
Grandma took a honey jar from the basket. She spread honey on bread and offered it toward Mumu. "Try this." He stretched his neck forward and took a bite. Sweetness filled his beak.
Grandma pointed to the stream. "Your mom splashed there when she was little too." "Mom too?" Mumu leaned his big head forward. Grandma's wing touched his back lightly. Warm.
Dodo whispered, "Grandma packed honey for you early this morning." Mumu stared at the big jar. "She packed it early... for me..."
Mumu's footprints led from behind the straw pile to here. "Grandma, hug me too!" He snuggled beneath her wing. "Into Grandma's wings!" One flick of his tail.
That evening in the yard, Grandma told old stories. Mumu under her left wing, Dodo under her right. Grandma didn't feel unfamiliar anymore.
The next morning, Mumu slipped under Grandma's wing first. "One, sit beside Grandma! Two, listen to her stories! Three, into Grandma's wings!" She lifted a wing a little to make room.
By the bridge, Grandma hugged both in her wings. "My little ducklings!" Unfamiliar at first, a hug soon brings fondness. Mumu hugged Grandma's neck and called, "Into Grandma's wings!"
